subject: Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs — MedSync discovery
messages:
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: samir.gupta@medsync.com; olivia.park@medsync.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs — MedSync discovery

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so your team has a single reference and to confirm next steps. Punch list below follows what we discussed.

Summary of what we heard
- Current pain: rising token costs and throttling limits on current provider (OpenAI paid plan + Anthropic for safety prompts). Production latency spikes during batch scoring windows.
- Risk/constraint: existing stack uses OpenAI chat endpoints for both assistant and reranking workflows; minimal on-prem infra today. Data residency must remain within US, PHI-sensitive flows for claims processing.
- Success criteria: parity on latency (p95 within 50ms of current peeks for short queries), 20–30% inferred cost reduction, and no degradation on reranker accuracy (measured by your current A/B prompt set).

Current stack details (as captured on call)
- Frontend -> API gateway -> microservice (Node) -> OpenAI chat/completions (primary) + Anthropic for safety transforms.
- Batch reranking pipeline: nightly job -> 2k items -> calls to OpenAI/small context reranker.
- Model sizes: mostly 7–13B for assistant; small 2–3B for embeddings not in scope today.

Compatibility & technical asks
- Requires support for chat-style assistant API semantics + tool calls (we discussed function-like structured responses).
- KV cache persistence across warm restarts (important for token-cost on long chat sessions).
- Quantized 4-bit or 8-bit runtime to hit cost targets without accuracy loss.
- Audit logs / request-level trace for HIPAA evidencing; will need to integrate with your Audit API.

Initial model shortlist we discussed
- Llama 2 (compatibility via chat format; candidate for assistant workloads)
- Mistral 7B Instruct (good cost/quality tradeoff for reranking)
- Falcon-40B Instruct (if you need to remain in high-quality headroom for hard edge cases)

Immediate next steps (agreed)
1) I will send a short Migration Assessment Plan (MAP) with: compatibility checklist, quantization options, and run cost estimates for your weekly volumes — ACTION: Ben (by Tue 11/17).
2) Schedule a 60m technical deep-dive with your infra/security + our runtime team to validate KV cache and logging approach — ACTION: Samir to propose two slots.
3) You to share a sample reranker prompt set + 20 representative examples (anonymized) so we can run a fast proof-of-concept (POC).

Attachments: I attached a one-page MAP and the draft cost worksheet for the volumes you quoted.

If I missed anything or misstated priorities, flag them and I’ll update.

Thanks — look forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: MedSync-Migration-Assessment.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: samir.gupta@medsync.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: olivia.park@medsync.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs — MedSync discovery

Ben — thanks for the crisp summary. Confirming a few clarifications from our side:

- Volume check: the reranker nightly batch is closer to 2.4k items currently (not 2k). Our assistant peaks at ~90 requests/minute during morning window.
- On PHI: not all payloads are PHI — roughly 40% of requests include PHI fields; we will redact when possible but need guaranteed network isolation for those flows.
- Compliance: we have to validate SOC2 plus a fed-level compliance packet for one enterprise partner — can your private deployment package be air-gapped for that?

Deliverables from our side
- I will (a) share the anonymized prompt set by EOD Wed 11/18, (b) loop in procurement for contract questions once we have cost estimates. Olivia will coordinate security questionnaire details.

For the deep-dive, propose Wed 11/18 11:00am PT or Thu 11/19 10:00am PT. Either works for the team — pick what works for yours.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Product, MedSync Health
samir.gupta@medsync.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs — MedSync discovery

Forwarding the discovery notes from MedSync. TL;DR: PHI in ~40% of requests, nightly reranker ~2.4k, assistant peak ~90rpm, needs KV cache persistence and audit logs.

What I need from you two before the deep-dive:
- Vanessa: can you draft an architecture sketch for a Private deployment option that supports network isolation + KMS integration (HSM optional)? Include proposed SLA and expected infra footprint for initial POC.
- Rishi: can you put together a short quantization + performance note comparing Llama 2, Mistral 7B, and Falcon-40B on expected token throughput and memory footprint (targeting 4-bit quant where feasible)? Also include rough latency p95 estimates for 90rpm peak.

I'll attach the MAP and the anonymized example list once Samir sends it.

Thanks — Ben
[Attachment: RWD-3491-MAP.pdf (pdf)]
From: olivia.park@medsync.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: samir.gupta@medsync.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs — MedSync discovery

Ben — small update from the security side: we will share the completed questionnaire by Thu 11/19. For scheduling the deep-dive, Wed 11/18 11:00am PT works best for our infra and security folks.

Also to confirm acceptance criteria for the POC:
- Must demonstrate parity on reranker accuracy (we will provide scoring script).
- Show KV cache persistence across node restarts in the POC environment.
- Demonstrate audit log export to our SIEM (we will provide S3 endpoint).

We'll upload the anonymized examples to the Drive folder you linked. Looking forward to the MAP.

Olivia Park
Head of Security Operations, MedSync Health
olivia.park@medsync.com
